corrected_value.title: Meta-analysis Confirms CR1, CLU, and PICALM as Alzheimer Disease Risk Loci and Reveals Interactions With APOE Genotypes

decisions.location: Methods (Statistical Analyses, line 209); Results (line 710); Discussion (line 713); References ([16], line 748)
decisions.quote: In a recently published article an interaction between PICALM (rs3851179) and APOEε4 was reported (interaction OR=0.84, unadjusted p=0.0068), but not between CR1 (rs3818361) and APOEε4 (interaction OR=1.01, unadjusted p=0.28) [16]. In our study, the test for interaction between PICALM and APOEε4 was not significant (OR=0.97, unadjusted p=0.74); however, it is possible that our sample was not of sufficient size to detect the interaction previously reported.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent. In addition to replicating the BIN1 (rs744373) and EXOC3L2 (rs597668) main-effect risk associations from Seshadri et al. (2010) [6] (shipped row 221, 10.1001/jama.2010.574), Carrasquillo et al. (2011) empirically test all 15 pairwise epistatic interactions among LOAD susceptibility SNPs and APOE ε4 in 3,287 LOAD cases and 4,396 controls and directly evaluate the previously reported positive interaction between PICALM (rs3851179) and APOE ε4 from Jun et al. (2010) [16] (10.1001/archneurol.2010.201), finding no significant interaction (OR=0.97, unadjusted p=0.74) and concluding in the Discussion that the PICALM * APOEε4 interaction reported previously by Jun et al. [16] did not replicate. Jun et al. (2010) is an independent original study absent from all shipped rows.
